messages:
rory: FYI customer reported weird behaviour when rotating keys that are mounted via secrets volume. long-lived stream immediately errored and the js sdk didn't pick up the new token even though the file was updated.

emma: Which SDK/lang and sampleapp? We have filewatching logic in python but JS only reads on startup AFAIK.

rory: sampleapp-node, sdk-js 0.9.2. The secret was updated in place (same path /etc/redwood/secret/token) and the file contents changed. Node process kept using old token until restart.

josh: Hmm this is by design for the JS runtime (no FS watcher) because of earlier perf/FD limits in containerized envs. But agree UX is bad for onboarding.

rory: Repro steps I used:
```
# start sampleapp
cat /etc/redwood/secret/token         # shows old token
# replace file with new token (kubectl cp or mount update)\n# observe stream error: 401 -> app keeps running but no reconnect
```

emma: Can we add an optional `REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE_WATCH=true` env flag to sdk-js to enable a polling-based reload? Keep it off by default to avoid surprise FD usage.

josh: I like that. Also add support for `SIGHUP` to trigger a manual reload for ops who prefer signal-based control. Example: `kill -HUP $(pidof sampleapp)` to reload creds from disk.

infra-bot: deploybot: sdk-js v0.9.2 deployed to staging 34 minutes ago (hash: bbccdd).

rory: Another twist: some teams use `RW_API_KEY` env var, others `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, and k8s secrets map to `/etc/redwood/secret/token`. The SDK needs a clear precedence and a short doc in the sampleapp.

emma: Proposed precedence: explicit SDK config object > env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` > env var `RW_API_KEY` > token file at `/etc/redwood/secret/token` > ~/.redwood/credentials. Document this and call out rotation semantics for each source.

josh: For streaming specifically, two approaches:
1) client-side: poll file or respond to SIGHUP and attempt seamless reconnect with resume token.
2) server-side: accept rotated key for a grace window and emit header `x-old-key-accept-seconds: <n>` on new connections. Server change is non-breaking.

rory: Server grace window would help other SDKs too. Ops likes deterministic short window (30s) but customers onboarding prefer longer (2m). We should default to 60s and make it configurable via account setting.

emma: I'll open an SDK PR adding `REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE_WATCH` + SIGHUP handler + docs and tests. Will gate with a feature-flag at runtime `REDWOOD_ENABLE_ROTATE_POLL` to avoid default behavior change.

josh: I'll add a small resume flow in js sdk: on auth failure, attempt up to 3 quick reload attempts (0, 200ms, 1s) and if creds change, try reconnecting with resume. If still 401, bubble error. Keep logs verbose only when `DEBUG=redwood:*`.

docs-bot: docs: added placeholder section "Credential sources and rotation" to quickstart (unpublished).

rory: Nice. Can someone add a short troubleshooting note to sampleapp README: "If using mounted secrets, enable file watch or restart on rotation" + a one-liner to SIGHUP.

emma: Will do. Also propose a tiny CLI helper to rotate creds in dev: `rw rotate --file /etc/redwood/secret/token --new <token>` that updates file and optionally sends SIGHUP to a PID file. Could be useful for e2e tests.

josh: Action items: emma -> SDK PR (file watch + SIGHUP + tests); rory -> sampleapp README + rotate helper script; infra -> discuss server-side grace header (50-60s default). I'll sketch the reconnect/resume code and open PR for review.

rory: Marking this P1 for DX but P0 for the specific customer. Thanks all :raised_hands:
